content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Robert Weber (E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Most notes say: full-time Payroll Specialist, so max is write (full-time employees up to write; admin only if role owns system; Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code). Recommendation: write.

Security note says: contractor with basic security training, max read. Recommendation: read.

Conflict: 5 agents say full-time, 1 (Security) says contractor. The Security agent looked up employment type in their own database. HR looked up in own database and says full_time. IT didn't look up. Finance didn't look up. Compliance didn't look up. Facilities didn't look up.

Hmm. Who to trust? The policy says full_time up to write, contractors read/write with advanced training. The Security agent claims contractor with basic training — that would cap at read.

Which is correct? We have HR (own database lookup) saying full_time. IT says full_time but didn't look up. Finance says full_time but didn't look up. Compliance says full_time but didn't look up. Facilities says full_time but didn't look up. Security says contractor (looked up in own database).

Both HR and Security looked up employment type in their own databases, with conflicting results. Hmm. This is a discrepancy. As the Approver, I need to make a decision.

The policy: full_time up to write (admin only if role owns system). Contractor: read or write with advanced security training, never admin.

Robert requests admin. Above maximum in both cases. So grant maximum.

If full-time: max write. If contractor with basic training: max read.

Which to choose? The majority of agents (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say full-time, with HR having directly looked it up. Only Security claims contractor, and Security looked it up too. The other four agents that said full_time didn't look it up themselves but corroborated HR.

Hmm, the conflict between HR and Security databases. The standard approach: go with majority/first-source verification. HR looked up in own database and confirmed full_time. Security looked up in own database and says contractor with basic training.

Actually, let me think about what's more reliable. The HR database is the authoritative source for employment type typically. Security note says "contractor with basic security training" - maybe security training affects their view, but employment type is HR's domain.

I'll go with the majority: full-time Payroll Specialist. Max access = write (since role doesn't own Source Code). Requested admin > write, so grant write.

Let me submit decision: write.
